instruction: Navigate to the Google Scholar page for the paper's corresponding author using Chrome.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('f11'); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.scroll(-40)

metadata.explanation: Paraphrase focusing on 'navigate to' instead of 'pull up'. The corresponding author is Tianlin (Tim) Shi with email tianlin@cs.stanford.edu and Google Scholar ID qRAQ5BsAAAAJ. Task requires the same steps as original: identify corresponding author from PDF, search Google Scholar, open profile. Evaluator uses existing is_expected_url_pattern_match metric.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator logic correctly verifies the core instruction requirement: navigating to the correct Google Scholar author page
Getter (get_active_url_from_accessTree) correctly extracts active Chrome tab URL from accessibility tree
Metric (is_expected_url_pattern_match) correctly performs regex pattern matching on all required patterns
Expected values are semantically correct: checks both Google Scholar citations URL and the specific author user ID (qRAQ5BsAAAAJ)
Complete coverage: evaluator checks both that user is on Google Scholar AND that it's the corresponding author's page
Pattern matching logic will work correctly at runtime with proper AND logic (all patterns must match)
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: Consider adding postconfig to ensure Chrome is the active/focused window before evaluation, as the setup opens a PDF which may leave Document Viewer in focus
Optional: The accessibility tree getter should work even if Chrome is not focused (as long as it's open), but adding a Chrome focus step would make evaluation more robust
